notes: Section 1.3 explicitly indicates treatment of esophageal candidiasis in adults and pediatric patients 2 years and older. The condition also occurs in adverse-reaction trial-population discussion. Such a safety-section mention does not contradict the indication. Review is limited to this label.

The matching passage inside section 1.11 discusses arthropathy and histopathological changes in weight-bearing joints of juvenile animals as adverse effects. It does not establish treatment of generic arthropathy. Bone/joint infections are separately listed as indications, so concept granularity and the original DrugCentral assertion also need review. This is a verified misleading text match, not a completed adjudication of all 261 cited labels or all possible uses.

The injection label explicitly indicates temporary control of rapid ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation/flutter, but contraindicates use when an accessory bypass tract is present (e.g. WPW). The same condition can appear in both indication and contraindication contexts. Formulation, treatment purpose and patient restrictions matter.

The indications text describes replacement/supplemental therapy for hypothyroidism of any etiology, subject to exceptions, while dosage has an explicit Congenital Hypothyroidism subsection. The precise phrase also appears under pediatric precautions. The automated safety-without-indication-name category is a wording/hierarchy limitation, not a demonstrated wrong indication.

Retinopathy of prematurity is an indication subsection heading beneath EYLEA is indicated for the treatment of, and has condition-specific dosing. Retaining title-only sections fixes an initial automated false negative.

Section 1.1 explicitly indicates treatment of mild to severe chronic heart failure of ischemic or cardiomyopathic origin. Section 5.4 warns that worsening heart failure or fluid retention may occur during dose up-titration. This is direct evidence that the condition can legitimately occur in both indications and warnings.

Section 1.2 explicitly indicates treatment of advanced/metastatic medullary thyroid cancer with a RET mutation, in adults and pediatric patients 2 years and older requiring systemic therapy. The lexical screen matches carcinoma in warnings but lacks the cancer synonym in indications. This is a terminology false negative, not evidence of an invalid indication.
